To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the intervention was effective in reducing institutionalization in patients with dementia and that this was achieved by a reduction in the rate of hospitalization.
the support programme for patients and caregivers with dementia was associated with lower institutionalisation rates.
the intervention did not lead to a significant reduction in institutionalization rates.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: the role of social support for caregivers and patients with dementia in the prevention of institutionalisation, the role of caregiver burden and the quality of life of caregivers, the development and evaluation of interventions for dementia patients and their caregivers, the evaluation of interventions in the context of dementia care and the role of the social environment of dementia patients and their carers in the prevention of depression.
the development of new materials and processes for the manufacture of micro- and nanoelectromechanical systems (MEMS and NEMS).
the social and economic aspects of dementia and the care of people with dementia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study did not show any significant effect of the intervention on institutionalization, mortality, or quality of life.
the intervention was successful in reducing the rate of nursing home admission for patients with dementia.
the intervention was effective in delaying the time to institutionalisation, but the effect was not sustained after the end of the intervention period.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the programme was successful in keeping the patients in their homes.
it is possible to delay the institutionalization of patients with dementia by providing support for caregivers, but the effect of the programme is not sustained over a period of 5 y.
the support programme for dementia patients and their caregivers lowered the risk for institutionalisation, but did not improve quality of life or cognitive function of the patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a new model for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease that is effective, affordable and sustainable.

the use of the Dementia Care Mapping tool in care homes is feasible and acceptable to care staff, and that it can be used as a tool to support care staff in the development of person-centred care for people with dementia.
a community-based, multidisciplinary support programme can be effective for delaying the need for institutionalisation in patients with dementia and for improving the well-being of their caregivers.
